previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening headaches, abdominal pain, and right calf pain. Imaging showed no acute intracranial or abdominal pathology; the headache was attributed to neck muscle spasms, and abdominal pain was likely due to a gastric ulcer. Her rapamycin level was elevated, prompting a dose reduction. Diabetes was diagnosed with an A1c of 7.5%, likely steroid-induced, and NPH insulin was initiated. Symptoms improved during the stay, and she was discharged home with updated medications and follow-up plans for oncology, ophthalmology, and endocrinology.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

# GI bleed: Patient reports approximately 1 week of melena and 
had brown guaiac positive stool on rectal exam in the ED. She 
was hemodynamically stable, but did have HCT 25.5 on admission 
from 37.5 two weeks prior to admission. She had a recent 
endoscopy with biopsies ___ which showed gastritis but no

signifying recent bleeding, colonoscopy showed sigmoid 
ulceration, neither felt to be clear source of bleed. Capsule 
study done, which also showed no source of bleeding. She was 
continued on BID PPI therapy and started on ampicillin and 
clarithromycin to complete a 2 week course for treatment of H. 
pylori.

# Anticoagulation: Patient with recurrent DVTs, PE in the past 
(last clot over 6 months prior to admission). Has been on 
Lovenox 60mg daily chronically. This was initially held in 
setting of GI bleed. Lower extremity ultrasounds showed no 
evidence of active clot. Patient with continued easy bruising 
and purpura off anticoagulation. This is most likely secondary 
to chronic steroid use, but platelet aggregation studies also 
sent which were still pending at the time of discharge. Given 
stable hematocrit and no signs of active bleeding, Lovenox 
restarted at 40mg daily dose the day prior to discharge.

# Transaminitis: patient has had intermittant elevation in LFTs 
since transplant. There is some thought that this may represent 
GVHD, although she has not had biopsy-proven GVHD of GI tract at 
this point. Recent liver ultrasound showed mildly increased 
echogenicity of liver without any focal lesions. LFTs stable 
through admission. Results of biopsy of sigmoid ulceration still 
pending at time of discharge.
   
# Oral lesions: patient with ulceration under the tongue, 
lesions on soft palate. HSV culture pending at time of 
discharge.

(including eyes, liver, ? stomach). Continued sirolimus (level 
pending at time of discharge), prednisone, as well as eye 
regimen of erythromycin ointment, latanoprost, cyclosporine

musculoskeletal. CT head without acute intracranial abnormality.
